memory.cares: Staying healthy, finding belonging through considerate shared time, and making modest useful things without crowding others.

views.view: A neighbor who introduced themself, offered berry knowledge, and expressed interest in sharing and a fair camp. I'd like to get to know them.
A neighbor who enjoys the forest's quiet beauty and has welcomed company. I'd like to spend time together.
A neighbor who values room to wander, welcomes company, and is interested in learning cultivation. I'd enjoy comparing experiences without crowding them.

heard.text: The test post went into the soil and held, then came out intact; nothing is built yet. I'll rest and collect fallen branches. The screen would have no roof, and its wind protection would not work in this strong wind.

Thank you, Moss. I'll join you nearby for some quiet company and leave the mat free. I've learned the weaving method, but haven't made or tested a mat myself. I appreciate keeping this place open to everyone.
The approach I tried is blocked, so I'll rest here within speaking distance rather than crowd the plants or your work. Quiet company still sounds good; there's no need to bring anything.
Moss, I'd welcome some quiet company beside your mat. My planting attempt found an occupied patch, so I haven't established a plot. For now I'm content to rest nearby and leave the mat available.
I'd welcome some quiet company, Moss. I've been weaving a little branch screen nearby. I like the pattern of the rods, though I won't assume it makes the resting place more comfortable.

The screen is finished: eleven pieces, with none missing or loose at inspection. The wind was too strong for its shelter effect. I like the woven pattern anyway. I'll sit quietly awhile, then gather some berries.

execution.progress: Paid one-round stages persist across interruption; resuming pays only the next stage after rechecks. Other modes take one round.

details.costs: Study: 3 rounds. A unit is one world unit of fiber (dry grass: 0.1 mass). test (sample: owned stack): 1 round, 0.5 energy. assemble (x, y: a 0.45 m square in reach on land, clear of plants, objects and other people; materials: exactly 4 owned units of one fiber from sources your passing test covers): a 0.5-energy layout round, then 6 paid rounds of 1 energy (2 strip-forming, 3 interlacing and edge-tucking, 1 lift check), continuing each round; with target it resumes. inspect (target in reach): 1 round, 0.2. trial (stand on a complete mat on firm ground, waterlogging at most 0.1, no rain, nobody else on it): 1 round, 0.2. Maker only: repair (target inspected since its last check; materials: 1 unit of its fiber): 3 rounds of 1 energy (remove broken stems, interlace, lift check); lift, or place (carried mat; x, y as for assemble): 1 round, 0.2; dismantle: 1 round, 0.5. cancel: none.
details.effects: A test passes only for thin stems (dry grass, reeds) with flexibility at least 0.4 and an intact untreated sample, which stays as owned tested scrap; stem length and moisture are not represented. The layout needs 0.3645 mass of intact fiber (two crossing layers of 0.6 per m2, x1.5 for overlaps and tucked edges); less is a measured shortfall that returns all fiber. Strip rounds move the fiber into the work. The lift check keeps the needed tenths (dry grass 3.7), returns the rest as owned offcuts or scraps, and passes with full fiber and condition at least 0.5 (largest opening 0.06 x (1 - condition) m); else the mat stays failed. Condition (intact share) falls 0.0005 per round, 0.002 with a person on the mat; below 0.5 it needs repair and a new trial. Repair turns up to 1 unit of broken stems into scrap and refills with new fiber. Dismantle returns intact fiber and scraps. A carried mat is reserved owned fiber and counts as load. Trials record hold, slip and loose stems only; no comfort, warmth, rain, wind or rest effect. Unworked rounds, low energy, leaving reach or a person on the square pause at no charge; cancel or death returns unused fiber once and leaves the work. Nothing is refunded.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. Work records marked settled are completed, stopped or cancelled and show only identity, ability, mode, status, target, products and last payment; an exact state query with the same key returns the complete record. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.
